title: U.S. House · Michigan's 5th District
area: Michigan's 5th Congressional District — south-central Michigan, including Jackson and parts of Lenawee and Hillsdale counties.

context.text: Cook Political Report rated Michigan's 5th District R+13 for the 2026 cycle. Donald Trump won the district 62.8%–35.8% in 2024.
Incumbent Tim Walberg was unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary. Christian Vukasovich was unopposed in the Democratic primary after Jacob Vravis left the race.

candidates.name: Tim Walberg
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, Michigan's 5th District (since 2023); in the U.S. House 2007–2009 and continuously since 2011

summary.text: Walberg is the incumbent U.S. Representative, representing the current 5th District since redistricting took effect in 2023. A minister and Moody Bible Institute manager who served 16 years in the Michigan House, he first took office in Congress in 2007, representing Michigan's 7th District from 2007 to 2009 and again from 2011 to 2023. He chairs the House Committee on Education and the Workforce.

background.text: Born in Chicago, Illinois, in 1951; attended Moody Bible Institute and earned a bachelor's degree from Fort Wayne Bible College (1975) and a master's degree from Wheaton College (1978).

According to his House website, he served as a pastor in Michigan and Indiana, as president of the Warren Reuther Center for Education and Community Impact, and as a division manager for Moody Bible Institute before entering public office.
Served in the Michigan House of Representatives from 1983 to 1999.
Took office in the U.S. House in January 2007 representing Michigan's 7th District (succeeding Joe Schwarz) and served until 2009, when Mark Schauer succeeded him in the seat.

Returned to the U.S. House in 2011 for the 7th District and, after redistricting, has represented the 5th District since 2023. His House website calls him the dean of the Michigan congressional delegation and says he is serving his ninth term.
In the 119th Congress he chairs the House Committee on Education and the Workforce and also serves on the Natural Resources Committee.

His House website says the Center for Effective Lawmaking, a Vanderbilt University and University of Virginia collaboration, ranked him the most effective member of Michigan's congressional delegation in the 115th Congress, and it cites his American Conservative Union lifetime score.
According to his House website, he and his wife, Sue, have been married for more than 50 years, have three children and seven grandchildren, and live in Tipton, Michigan.

priorities.text: Creating long-term job growth in Michigan is my top priority in Congress.
Congress needs to manage its spending just like many hard-working, honest families and businesses back in Michigan who work every day towards maintaining their responsible bottom lines.
As a member of Congress I have consistently supported legislative initiatives that would give the states, parents, and teachers the ability to determine the educational needs of our children.

positions.summary: Says the U.S. must secure the border and enforce immigration law, and voted for legislation funding thousands of additional ICE, Border Patrol and customs personnel and for the Laken Riley Act requiring ICE to detain certain criminal aliens.
positions.quote: we must secure our borders, enforce our laws, and cut unnecessary red tape for legal immigration

positions.summary: Says he holds the sanctity of life in the highest regard and supports legislation protecting the rights of the unborn; cosponsored the No Taxpayer Funding for Abortion and Abortion Insurance Full Disclosure Act.
positions.quote: I hold the sanctity of life in the highest regard and will continue to work diligently and support legislation that protects the rights of the unborn.

positions.summary: Supports the right of law-abiding citizens to bear arms and has cosponsored bills including the Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act and the Hearing Protection Act.
positions.quote: I support the right for law abiding citizens to bear arms and will continue to defend this liberty throughout my service in Congress.

positions.summary: Says Michigan parents should be able to choose their children's school and supports federal scholarships allowing students at failing schools to attend a different educational institution.
positions.quote: Michigan parents should have the opportunity to choose the type of education their children receive. If federal scholarships are made available to some students in failing schools, they should be allowed to attend the educational institution of their choice, free from government interference.

positions.summary: Says the U.S. must continue to stand with Israel and has cosponsored measures including the United States-Israel Defense Partnership Act.
positions.quote: we must continue to stand with Israel as they defend themselves

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025–2026), serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources (Indian and Insular Affairs; Water, Wildlife and Fisheries) and chairs the House Committee on Education and the Workforce.
Cosponsored H.R. 7, the No Taxpayer Funding for Abortion and Abortion Insurance Full Disclosure Act, introduced January 2025.
Cosponsored H.R. 38, the Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act, introduced January 2025.

candidates.name: Christian Vukasovich
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary

summary.text: Vukasovich is a teacher and college professor who was born in Michigan. He was unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary and is the Democratic nominee against incumbent Tim Walberg.

background.text: Worked as a teacher and a college professor.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website located; background limited to what Ballotpedia's biography section documents.

candidates.name: James Bronke

summary.text: Bronke is the Green Party nominee for Michigan's 5th District, advancing from the Green Party convention on April 25, 2026. He is an engineer by profession.

background.text: Born in Manchester, Connecticut; earned a high school diploma from George J. Penney High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from California State University, Northridge (1982).
Works as an engineer and has been associated with the Eagles Club.

candidates.name: Ronald Muszynski

summary.text: Muszynski is the Libertarian Party nominee for Michigan's 5th District, nominated at the party's June 28, 2026 convention. He has appeared on Michigan ballots as a candidate for the state legislature in earlier elections.

background.text: Was the Libertarian candidate for Michigan State Senate District 17 in 2010 and lost the general election to incumbent Randy Richardville (R).
Was a candidate in the 2016 general election for Michigan House of Representatives District 65, won by incumbent Brett Roberts.
Was the Libertarian candidate for Michigan State Senate District 16 in 2018, losing the general election to incumbent Mike Shirkey (R).

candidates.name: Sharon Renier

summary.text: Renier is the U.S. Taxpayers Party nominee for Michigan's 5th District, advancing from the party's convention on July 18, 2026. She previously sought the Republican nomination for the Michigan House of Representatives.

background.text: Ran in the August 3, 2010 Republican primary for the Michigan House of Representatives and was defeated by Mike Shirkey.
